metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (index.php) with a deployable entry point (PHP Apache server), Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, and CloudFormation IaC provisioning AWS resources. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: MySQL database with 9 tables, CRUD endpoints for orders/inventory/payments/returns/users, entity lifecycle management (order status transitions), user-specific data. Classified as stateful-crud.

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with all domains in a single 1800+ line PHP file, shared database, no module boundaries
top_gaps.impact: Cannot scale domains independently, no team autonomy, deployment coupling blocks modernization

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipeline — deployment is a manual bash script wrapping docker-compose
top_gaps.impact: Manual deployments are error-prone, slow, and prevent continuous delivery

top_gaps.title: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: No deployment strategy — manual docker-compose deploy with no staged rollout
top_gaps.impact: No ability to safely release changes, no rollback capability, high blast radius

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.gap: No automated tests of any kind — no unit tests, no integration tests
top_gaps.impact: Cannot validate changes before deployment, high regression risk

top_gaps.title: Unstructured Data Storage
top_gaps.gap: No S3 or managed object storage for documents/unstructured data
top_gaps.impact: Data locked in MySQL only, no document parsing or analytics capability

findings.title: Managed Compute — partial adoption
findings.description: Application runs on AWS App Runner (managed container service) with auto-scaling. Basic concurrency-based scaling only with single service deployment.
findings.gap: App Runner configured with basic concurrency-based scaling only. No custom scaling policies. Single service deployment — no multi-service compute optimization.
findings.recommendation: Consider migrating to ECS/EKS as the application is decomposed into microservices for more granular scaling control per service.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — all logic hardcoded
findings.description: Complex multi-step order fulfillment workflow (confirm→validate→assign warehouse→pick→pack→QC→ship→deliver) entirely hardcoded in index.php with no dedicated orchestration service.
findings.gap: All workflow logic hardcoded in application code with no retry logic, no error handling orchestration, no visual workflow management.
findings.recommendation: Adopt AWS Step Functions for the order fulfillment workflow. Provides visual workflow management, automatic retry/error handling, and state management.

findings.title: Async Messaging — no messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. All state changes occur synchronously within the PHP process. For a stateful-crud service, synchronous-only coupling where state changes cross domain boundaries is an anti-pattern.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Return processing requires 24-48 hour async handling but has no queue infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS for async processing of returns and cross-domain notifications. Use EventBridge for event-driven communication between extracted services.

findings.title: Network Security — good segmentation, no managed networking services
findings.description: Services in custom VPC with private subnets for RDS. Least-privilege security groups. VPC Flow Logs with KMS encryption.
findings.gap: No managed networking services layered on top (no VPC endpoints, no PrivateLink, no VPC Lattice).
findings.recommendation: Add VPC endpoints for AWS services (ECR, CloudWatch). Consider VPC Lattice for service-to-service communication during decomposition.

findings.title: API Entry Point — WAF with managed rules, no API Gateway
findings.description: WAFv2 Web ACL with IP whitelisting and AWS Managed Rules. App Runner provides built-in load balancing.
findings.gap: No full API Gateway with request validation, throttling per-route, or API key management.
findings.recommendation: Add API Gateway in front of services for throttling, request validation, and centralized API management when decomposing into microservices.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — basic default configuration only
findings.description: App Runner auto-scaling with MinSize=1, MaxSize=3, MaxConcurrency=100. Basic concurrency-based scaling only.
findings.gap: Default scaling settings only. No custom policies based on business metrics. No data layer scaling.
findings.recommendation: Configure RDS read replicas with auto-scaling. Adjust App Runner thresholds based on traffic patterns. Consider Aurora Serverless.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — automated but incomplete
findings.description: RDS automated backups with 7-day retention. DeletionPolicy: Snapshot ensures data preservation.
findings.gap: No PITR explicitly configured. No documented restore testing. No cross-region backup replication.
findings.recommendation: Enable PITR for RDS. Document and test restore procedures. Add AWS Backup plan for centralized management.

findings.title: IaC Coverage — primary resources covered, operational resources missing
findings.description: CloudFormation covers VPC, RDS, App Runner, WAF, ECR, KMS, IAM. No operational/DR resources in IaC.
findings.gap: No CloudWatch alarms, Route 53 health checks, or AWS Backup plans in IaC. Monitoring and observability resources absent.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms, Route 53 health checks, and AWS Backup plans to CloudFormation template.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment is a manual bash script (deploy.sh) running docker-compose. Production deployment is manual CLI commands.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy. No pipeline definition files found.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with automated Docker build, ECR push, test execution, and App Runner deployment. Use CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions.

findings.title: Programming Languages — PHP with limited cloud-native tooling
findings.description: PHP 8.2 with Apache. Functional AWS SDK but limited cloud-native tooling depth. No dependency management (no Composer).
findings.gap: PHP has narrower cloud-native tooling compared to Python, Node.js, Go, or Java. No Composer dependency management.
findings.recommendation: For new services during decomposition, consider Python, Node.js/TypeScript, or Go. Existing PHP monolith can be maintained while new services use modern languages.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — tightly-coupled monolith
findings.description: Single index.php file (1800+ lines) containing all business logic for orders, inventory, payments, returns, users, warehouses. All domains share a single MySQL database. Cross-domain transactions pervasive.
findings.gap: Pervasive shared state, no module boundaries, no separation of concerns. Cannot scale domains independently.
findings.recommendation: Decompose using Strangler Fig pattern. Priority extraction: Inventory, then Orders/Payments. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — all synchronous
findings.description: All communication synchronous within single PHP process. No async patterns, no message queues, no event-driven handlers.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns. State changes that should be decoupled are tightly coupled synchronous operations.
findings.recommendation: Introduce EventBridge for cross-service notification. Use SQS for async return processing. Implement event-driven patterns for order status changes.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — all operations synchronous
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Return approval requires 24-48 hours manual review with no async infrastructure. Multi-step fulfillment has no background automation.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No queue or async job system for long-running processes.
findings.recommendation: Implement SQS-based async job processing for returns. Use Step Functions for multi-step fulfillment. Add status polling for long-running operations.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — no versioning
findings.description: No API versioning. All endpoints unversioned (/api/products, /api/orders, /api/returns). No URL-based, header-based, or query parameter versioning.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly with no backward compatibility.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-based API versioning (e.g., /api/v1/products) before decomposition.

findings.title: Service Discovery — no mechanism
findings.description: All service endpoints within single monolith. Database endpoint hardcoded via environment variable. No service registry or API catalog.
findings.gap: No service discovery mechanism for when the application is decomposed into microservices.
findings.recommendation: Implement AWS Cloud Map or ECS Service Discovery when decomposing. Use environment-based discovery as starting point.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — no S3 or object storage
findings.description: No S3 or managed object storage. All data in MySQL only. Product images referenced by URL path with no file storage infrastructure.
findings.gap: Data locked in MySQL only. No managed object storage for documents, images, or unstructured data.
findings.recommendation: Introduce S3 for product images, order documents, unstructured data. Add CloudFront for image delivery.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — centralized connection, scattered queries
findings.description: Centralized get_db() function provides connection. PDO used consistently. However, SQL queries scattered across all 27+ API handlers with no repository/DAO pattern.
findings.gap: Repository/DAO pattern absent. Direct SQL in every endpoint with no abstraction layer.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/DAO pattern per domain during decomposition. Each service should have a dedicated data access layer.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — mixed approach
findings.description: RDS StorageEncrypted with AWS-managed key. ECR and VPC Flow Logs use customer-managed KMS keys with rotation.
findings.gap: RDS uses AWS-managed encryption rather than customer-managed KMS key. Mixed encryption approach.
findings.recommendation: Consider migrating RDS to customer-managed KMS key. Document key rotation policies.

findings.title: API Authentication — session-based, no OAuth2/JWT
findings.description: PHP session-based authentication on all API endpoints. Username/password with bcrypt. Role-based access control. No token-based auth.
findings.gap: Session-based auth without OAuth2/JWT. No API Gateway authorizer integration.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to JWT/OAuth2 with Amazon Cognito when decomposing into microservices.

findings.title: Centralized Identity — no external IdP
findings.description: Application manages its own authentication entirely. Custom users table with bcrypt. No OIDC/SAML. No Cognito. No external IdP.
findings.gap: No external IdP integration. No SSO. Custom password management increases attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito for centralized identity, OAuth2/JWT, SSO, MFA, and federated identity.

findings.title: Secrets Management — env vars without rotation
findings.description: No plaintext credentials in source. Credentials via environment variables and CloudFormation NoEcho parameters. No Secrets Manager or rotation.
findings.gap: Production credentials in env vars and NoEcho parameters without Secrets Manager or rotation.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Use dynamic references in CloudFormation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — basic container security only
findings.description: ECR scan-on-push enabled. Non-root user in Dockerfile. no-new-privileges and read-only filesystem in docker-compose.
findings.gap: No proactive patching strategy. Default base image without hardening. No Dependabot/Renovate.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot/Renovate. Consider distroless base image. Enable ECR enhanced scanning.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools in any pipeline. No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. ECR scan-on-push only outside pipeline context.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. No Dependabot. No SAST. No security gates.
findings.recommendation: Add Dependabot, SAST (Semgrep/CodeGuru), container scanning, and security gates to CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no instrumentation
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray SDK, no OpenTelemetry, no trace ID propagation.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Debugging requires manual log correlation.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry. App Runner supports X-Ray natively.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — none defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions. No CloudWatch alarms. No availability targets. No monitoring artifacts.
findings.gap: No SLOs. No error budget tracking. No latency or availability alarms.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for critical journeys. Add CloudWatch alarms on p99 latency and error rate.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No CloudWatch PutMetricData. No business outcome tracking.
findings.gap: No custom metrics. Only default App Runner infrastructure metrics.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics for orders/hour, completion rate, return rate, fulfillment time.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — none configured
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms. No anomaly detection. No notification integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures go undetected until customer reports.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms for App Runner latency, error rate, and RDS metrics. Enable anomaly detection.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — direct-to-production
findings.description: No deployment strategy. deploy.sh runs docker-compose up -d. No staged rollout, no health check gate, no rollback.
findings.gap: Direct-to-production with no canary, blue/green, or rolling deployment.
findings.recommendation: Implement blue/green or canary using App Runner rolling updates. Add automated rollback on health check failure.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no tests exist
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. No test files, no PHPUnit, no API tests, no test framework.
findings.gap: No integration tests. Cannot validate changes before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add PHPUnit tests, API integration tests, test containers for MySQL. Add test execution to CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — no runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks. No incident response automation. No SSM documents. No self-healing patterns.
findings.gap: Incident response entirely ad hoc. No documented procedures.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents. Implement SSM Automation for known failure modes.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — none defined
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards. No alarms with owners. No CODEOWNERS. No SLO team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership. Monitoring reactive and fragmented.
findings.recommendation: Define service ownership with CODEOWNERS. Create CloudWatch dashboards. Assign alarm ownership.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance — inconsistent
findings.description: Some resources have Name and Environment tags. Tagging inconsistent — not all resources tagged, no cost allocation or ownership tags.
findings.gap: Inconsistent tagging. No standard. No enforcement. No cost allocation tags.
findings.recommendation: Define tagging standard. Add default tags to all resources. Implement AWS Config rules for enforcement.
